1.summary: Paul blesses God for every spiritual blessing in Christ: chosen, adopted, redeemed, sealed with the Spirit, as part of a plan to unite all things in Christ; then he prays that they would know the hope, riches and power of God that raised Jesus and made him head over all things for the church.
1.lookfor: Notice the repeated phrase "in Christ" or "in him," and how the blessing works through Father, Son and Spirit.

names.name: Ephesus
names.gloss: The leading city of the province of Asia.

insights.title: One long sentence
insights.body: In Greek, verses 3 to 14 are a single sentence of over 200 words, a cascade of praise in the style of a Jewish blessing that begins Blessed be God.

insights.title: In Christ
insights.body: In Christ, in him or in the Beloved appears about a dozen times in the opening blessing. Every blessing is found in union with Christ.

insights.title: Chosen before creation
insights.body: God chose us in him before the foundation of the world, to be holy and blameless (1:4). Election here is in Christ and for holiness, a reason for praise, not pride.

insights.title: Summing up all things
insights.body: God's plan for the fullness of the times is to sum up all things in Christ, things in heaven and things on earth (1:10). The word means to head up, gather under one head.

insights.title: Sealed
insights.body: You were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit (1:13). A seal marked ownership and guaranteed authenticity; the Spirit is also the down payment on our inheritance (1:14).

insights.title: Far above all rule
insights.body: God raised Christ and seated him at his right hand, far above all rule and authority, and put all things under his feet (1:20-22), drawing on Psalms 110 and 8.

insights.title: Eyes of the heart
insights.body: Paul prays that the eyes of your heart be enlightened (1:18). What do you most need God to open your eyes to see?

2.summary: Once dead in sins, we have been made alive and raised with Christ by grace through faith, not by works, to do good works; Gentiles once far off have been brought near, for Christ broke down the dividing wall and made Jews and Gentiles one new humanity, a holy temple.
2.lookfor: Notice the before and after ("once" and "but now"), and the picture of a wall torn down.

names.name: Gentiles
names.gloss: Non-Jewish nations, once excluded from Israel's covenants.

insights.title: Dead, then alive
insights.body: You were dead in trespasses and sins (2:1). Not sick or weak, dead. But God, rich in mercy, made us alive together with Christ (2:4-5). The turning point is two words: but God.

insights.title: By grace through faith
insights.body: By grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, so no one can boast (2:8-9). Perhaps the clearest summary of the gospel in Paul.

insights.title: Workmanship
insights.body: We are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works (2:10). The word is poiēma, the root of poem: a crafted work. Good works don't earn salvation; they are what salvation produces.

insights.title: The dividing wall
insights.body: Christ broke down the middle wall of separation (2:14). The temple had a barrier with warning inscriptions forbidding Gentiles to go further on pain of death. Paul was arrested over a rumor that he had brought a Gentile past it.

insights.title: Peace to those far and near
insights.body: He came and preached peace to you who were far off and to those who were near (2:17), echoing Isaiah's promise of peace to the far and the near.

insights.title: One new humanity
insights.body: Christ created in himself one new man out of the two (2:15). Not Gentiles becoming Jews or Jews becoming Gentiles, but a new people with access in one Spirit to the Father.

insights.title: Walls
insights.body: Christ tore down the wall between bitter enemies. What wall between you and another person or group does he want to bring down?

3.summary: Paul, a prisoner for the Gentiles, explains the mystery now revealed: that Gentiles are fellow heirs in Christ, and that through the church God's wisdom is shown to heavenly powers; he prays that they would be strengthened and grasp the immeasurable love of Christ.
3.lookfor: Notice how Paul defines the mystery, and the four dimensions of Christ's love in his prayer.

names.name: Gentiles
names.gloss: Those for whose sake Paul is imprisoned.

insights.title: Mystery
insights.body: In Paul, mystery doesn't mean something puzzling but something once hidden and now revealed (3:3-5). The mystery: Gentiles are fellow heirs, fellow members of the body, sharers in the promise (3:6).

insights.title: Less than the least
insights.body: Paul calls himself less than the least of all saints (3:8). He coins a word, a comparative of least, to describe himself.

insights.title: Wisdom on display
insights.body: Through the church, God's manifold wisdom is now made known to rulers and authorities in the heavenly places (3:10). A united church of former enemies is God's exhibit to the universe.

insights.title: Bowing the knee
insights.body: I bow my knees to the Father (3:14). Jews usually prayed standing; kneeling expressed special urgency or humility.

insights.title: Breadth, length, height, depth
insights.body: Paul prays they may grasp the breadth, length, height and depth of Christ's love, and know the love that surpasses knowledge (3:18-19). Love can be known but never measured.

insights.title: Far more than we ask
insights.body: God is able to do far more abundantly than all we ask or think (3:20). Paul's prayer ends in doxology because the God he prays to exceeds his requests.

insights.title: Rooted in love
insights.body: Paul prays that they be rooted and grounded in love (3:17). What would it mean for you to be rooted in God's love, not just to know about it?

4.summary: Paul urges them to walk worthy of their calling by keeping the unity of the Spirit, explains that Christ gave gifted leaders to equip the saints so the body grows to maturity, and calls them to put off the old self and put on the new, speaking truth and forgiving as God forgave them.
4.lookfor: Notice the seven "ones" in verses 4 to 6, and the put off and put on pattern.

insights.title: Walk worthy
insights.body: Chapters 1 to 3 told what God has done; now Paul says, therefore walk worthy of the calling (4:1). Behavior grows out of identity.

insights.title: Seven ones
insights.body: One body, one Spirit, one hope, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all (4:4-6). Unity is not created by us; we keep what the Spirit has made.

insights.title: He gave gifts
insights.body: Paul adapts Psalm 68: when he ascended on high, he led captivity captive and gave gifts to people (4:8). The victorious king distributes the spoils to his people.

insights.title: Equipping the saints
insights.body: Apostles, prophets, evangelists, shepherds and teachers are given to equip the saints for the work of ministry (4:11-12). Leaders train; everyone ministers.

insights.title: Old self, new self
insights.body: Put off the old man and put on the new (4:22-24), like changing clothes. New converts may have changed into white robes at baptism, picturing this exchange.

insights.title: Be angry and don't sin
insights.body: Be angry, and don't sin (4:26), quoting the Greek of Psalm 4. Anger itself isn't sin, but don't let the sun go down on it, or you give the devil a foothold.

insights.title: Forgive as forgiven
insights.body: Be kind, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ forgave you (4:32). Whom do you need to forgive in light of how much you've been forgiven?

5.summary: Paul calls believers to imitate God, walking in love and light, avoiding immorality and empty words, making the most of time, being filled with the Spirit, and submitting to one another; he describes marriage as a picture of Christ's love for the church.
5.lookfor: Notice the contrast between darkness and light, and how the husband's role is defined by Christ's self-giving.

insights.title: Imitators of God
insights.body: Be imitators of God, as beloved children, and walk in love as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us, a fragrant offering (5:1-2). Children copy the parents they love.

insights.title: Children of light
insights.body: You were once darkness, but now are light in the Lord (5:8). Ephesus was famous for magic and mystery cults that met at night; Paul calls believers to live openly.

insights.title: Redeeming the time
insights.body: Redeem the time, because the days are evil (5:16). Redeem means to buy up, like a merchant snapping up a bargain: seize every opportunity.

insights.title: Wine or Spirit
insights.body: Don't be drunk with wine, but be filled with the Spirit (5:18). Both influence behavior; the Spirit's filling shows in singing, thanksgiving and mutual submission (5:19-21).

insights.title: Submitting to one another
insights.body: Paul's household instructions begin with submit to one another in the fear of Christ (5:21). Roman household codes ran only one way, commanding wives, children and slaves; Paul gives husbands, fathers and masters duties too.

insights.title: A great mystery
insights.body: Husbands, love your wives as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her (5:25). The two become one flesh, a mystery that points to Christ and the church (5:31-32).

insights.title: Making the most of time
insights.body: Paul urges careful living and wise use of time. Where is your time leaking away, and how could you redeem it?

6.summary: Paul gives instructions to children, fathers, slaves and masters, then calls believers to be strong in the Lord and put on God's full armor to stand against the devil's schemes, praying always, including for Paul's boldness in chains.
6.lookfor: Notice how each piece of armor is defined, and that the real enemy isn't flesh and blood.

names.name: Tychicus
names.gloss: A beloved brother from Asia who carried the letter.

insights.title: Honor your parents
insights.body: Honor your father and mother, the first commandment with a promise (6:2), from the Ten Commandments. Fathers, in turn, must not provoke children to anger (6:4).

insights.title: Slaves and masters
insights.body: Paul tells slaves to serve as to Christ, and masters to stop threatening, knowing both have the same Master in heaven who shows no favoritism (6:5-9). He didn't overturn the system at once, but the seed that would undo it is here.

insights.title: Not flesh and blood
insights.body: Our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against principalities and powers, spiritual forces of evil (6:12). People are not the ultimate enemy.

insights.title: A soldier's kit
insights.body: Paul, chained to a Roman soldier, describes the armor: belt, breastplate, shoes, shield, helmet and sword (6:14-17). The large Roman shield could be soaked to quench fire-tipped arrows.

insights.title: God's own armor
insights.body: The armor is God's: Isaiah pictures the Lord himself putting on righteousness as a breastplate and salvation as a helmet (6:14, 6:17). Believers wear what God wears.

insights.title: An ambassador in chains
insights.body: Paul calls himself an ambassador in chains (6:20). Ambassadors were meant to be untouchable; Christ's envoy is in prison, yet asks only for boldness to speak.

insights.title: Stand
insights.body: The key word of the armor passage is stand (6:11, 6:13, 6:14). The battle is not to conquer new ground but to hold the ground Christ has already won.

insights.title: Which piece is missing?
insights.body: Look at the armor: truth, righteousness, peace, faith, salvation, the word, prayer. Which piece have you been going without?

intro.who: The letter names Paul as its author, writing as a prisoner (3:1, 4:1). Some scholars think a follower wrote it in his name, because its style differs from his earlier letters; many hold that Paul wrote it.
intro.when: About AD 60–62, during Paul's imprisonment, probably in Rome, sent with Tychicus along with Colossians and Philemon (6:21).
intro.why: Some early manuscripts lack "in Ephesus" (1:1), so it may have been a circular letter to churches in Asia. It celebrates God's plan to unite all things in Christ, shows Jews and Gentiles made one new people, and calls the church to live out that unity.

outline.title: What God has done: blessed, raised, made one
How to live: unity, holiness, households, armor
